context: The line he repeats from Extreme Ownership, the book he wrote with Leif Babin, and the title of his later field manual.

text: There are no bad teams, only bad leaders.
context: He calls this a fundamental truth of Extreme Ownership: the result belongs to the leader.

text: It's not what you preach, it's what you tolerate.
context: From Extreme Ownership. A standard that is announced and then accepted when broken is no longer the standard.

text: Leaders must own everything in their world. There is no one else to blame.
context: The book's opening principle, stated beside the name Extreme Ownership.

text: On any team, in any organization, all responsibility for success and failure rests with the leader.
context: The sentence that puts both the win and the loss on the same desk.

text: The leader must acknowledge mistakes and admit failures, take ownership of them, and develop a plan to win.
context: Ownership, in the book, is not a confession that stops. It ends in a plan.

text: But, in fact, discipline is the pathway to freedom.
context: His answer to the idea that discipline and freedom are opposites.

text: Ego clouds and disrupts everything: the planning process, the ability to take good advice, and the ability to accept constructive criticism.
context: From the ego principle in Extreme Ownership. The cloud is not confidence. It is the refusal to be corrected.

text: When setting expectations, no matter what has been said or written, if substandard performance is accepted and no one is held accountable — if there are no consequences — that poor performance becomes the new standard.
context: The book follows this with the requirement that leaders enforce standards.

text: The moment the alarm goes off is the first test; it sets the tone for the rest of the day.
context: Discipline, in the book, starts when the alarm goes off, not when the day becomes interesting.

text: How do I deal with setbacks, failures, delays, defeats, or other disasters? I actually have a fairly simple way of dealing with these situations, summed up in one word: Good.
context: The opening of the Good segment on Jocko Podcast episode 3, later printed in Discipline Equals Freedom.

text: So get up, dust off, reload, recalibrate, re-engage — and go out on the attack.
context: The close of that segment. The word Good is not cheerfulness. It is the turn back toward the problem.
